findings.title: CookieFactoryHook resolves Cookie by a class-name string instead of a class literal
findings.description: Known item (a), mostly refuted: ProGuard and R8 recognise Class.forName with a constant string and adapt the string when they rename the class, and the -keepclassmembers rule keeps the name of Cookie.unvalidated, so a standard minified build keeps working. The remaining risk is reliance on that string-adaptation heuristic (a tool or rule set without it); if it fails, the static initializer throws ExceptionInInitializerError and every req.cookie()/req.getCookies() call answers 500. Cookie is already imported and only the method needs reflection, so the string lookup buys nothing; the comment 'Class.forName also initialises Cookie' gives a reason nobody needs.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Cookie.class.getDeclaredMethod("unvalidated", String.class, String.class) and drop the Class.forName comment; every shrinker rewrites the class literal and the existing -keepclassmembers rule then fully covers the reflective use.

findings.title: Cookie parser drops a pair with whitespace around '=' instead of trimming name and value
findings.description: Only the whole pair is trimmed, so 'a = 1' yields the name 'a ' which fails isToken and the cookie is dropped silently. RFC 6265 section 5.2 and the Express 'cookie' parser trim name and value separately. FR-COOKIE-002 AC-4 only requires trimming around each pair, so this matches the spec; browsers do not send spaces around '=', so impact is limited to hand-written clients.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: trim name and value separately (pair.substring(0, eq).trim(), pair.substring(eq + 1).trim()) with one CookieParserTest case; otherwise keep and record the choice in docs/api.
